newsitem.title: USA: ITT seeks to stop Hilton challenge of plan.
newsitem.headline: ITT seeks to stop Hilton challenge of plan.

text.p: ITT Corp has launched a pre-emptive strike against hostile bidder Hilton Hotels Corp in an effort to prohibit it from trying to block a massive restructuring.
The hotel and casino giant has asked a federal judge to determine it has the right to pursue the plan that calls for ITT to split into three companies.
In court papers filed before U.S. District Court Judge Philip Pro, ITT said it was making the request in the belief that Hilton would challenge the plan.
"Despite the merits of the plan, Hilton's litigation record to date makes it highly likely that Hilton will seek to challenge the plan," ITT said in the court papers.
Hilton has lost several court fights aimed at forcing the takeover effort to move forward.

The filing was made Wednesday in Las Vegas before U.S. District Court Judge Philip Pro, who has handled other matters relating to the hostile takeover. The two companies have been locked in legal battles since Hilton launched the hostile $6.5 billion bid in January.
Indeed, Hilton on Wednesday vowed to pursue options against the ITT plan, but did not outline its strategy. So far, it has not filed any lawsuit against the plan.
A spokesman for Hilton declined to comment on the ITT court action, referring only to Wednesday's statement.
ITT has repeatedly rejected Hilton's bid and in recent months has generaed a huge cash stockpiling by selling non-core assets.

On Wednesday, ITT announced a long-awaited stock buyback and unveiled plans to split into three companies containing its prized hotel and casino business, its highly-profitable telephone directories unit and a group of technical schools.
In the court filing, ITT contends that Hilton cannot show that the plan violates Nevada law or that ITT's board acted outside of its power by approving the plan.
"It would be illogical if the board could not pursue the plan now, particularly given the threats to ITT posed by the Hilton bid," ITT said.
ITT also said it intends to pursue the restructuring plan, even if Hilton withdraws its bid for the company.
